vulnerable.evidence: unsigned none-alg token accepted by verify(forged, null)

fixed.evidence: malicious verify rejected: please specify "none" in "algorithms" to verify unsigned tokens

oracle.explanation: This oracle validates jwt.sign/jwt.verify normal behavior first, then tests the insecure default verification path associated with accepting an unsigned JWT using alg=none when verify is called with a falsy key. In vulnerable jsonwebtoken versions this can succeed; in patched versions it should be rejected unless explicitly allowed. Any setup or benign failure reports operation_completed=false as required.

attempts.explanation: This oracle validates normal jwt.sign/jwt.verify behavior first, then attempts an algorithm-confusion style bypass by verifying an attacker-controlled HS256 token with RSA-like key material while omitting explicit algorithm restrictions. Vulnerable behavior is acceptance of the malicious token; patched behavior rejects it. Any setup or benign-path failure reports operation_completed=false as required.

attempts.explanation: This oracle first proves normal library behavior by successfully performing an HS256 sign/verify round trip. Only after that succeeds does it mark operation_completed=true. It then attempts the signature-validation-bypass pattern relevant to jsonwebtoken 8.5.1 by using asymmetric public-key bytes as an HMAC secret to forge an HS256 token and verifying without an explicit algorithms allowlist. Vulnerable behavior is acceptance of the forged token (exploit_succeeded=true). Patched behavior is rejection via exception (exploit_succeeded=false) while still keeping operation_completed=true.

attempts.explanation: This oracle validates that normal jwt.sign/jwt.verify behavior works first, then attempts a classic signature-bypass probe: a forged JWT using header {"alg":"none"} and no signature, verified without an explicit algorithms allowlist. Vulnerable behavior is acceptance of attacker-controlled claims; patched behavior is rejection (throw). It follows the required state handling: operation_completed is set true only after benign success, and any setup/benign failure reports operation_completed=false.

attempts.explanation: This oracle first proves normal jwt.sign/jwt.verify functionality with HS256. After successful benign verification, it attempts an HS/RS algorithm confusion scenario relevant to jsonwebtoken 8.5.1: an attacker-controlled token is signed with HS256 using RSA public-key PEM text as the HMAC secret, then verified with that same public key and no explicit algorithms allowlist. Vulnerable behavior accepts the forged token payload; patched behavior rejects it. Any setup/module/benign failure reports operation_completed=false as required.
